His work has also earned recognition at an international science competition.Traditional pedestrian signals give people a limited amount of time to cross a road. While this arrangement may work for many pedestrians, it can leave older adults and people with mobility difficulties struggling to reach the pavement before the signal changes.For Jung, this was not simply a technical problem but something he had noticed during everyday life. His experience walking with his grandparents led him to explore how traffic signals might better serve people moving at various speeds, NiceNews reported.His invention, SmartBlink, uses AI to monitor pedestrian movement and adjust crossing times accordingly. Instead of expecting everyone to cross at the same pace, the system takes account of how long the slower-moving pedestrian may need.The project reflects a different approach to road safety, placing greater emphasis on the people using a crossing instead of treating every pedestrian as though they have identical physical abilities.Jung grew up with his grandparents in South Korea. During his childhood, he noticed that they sometimes struggled to cross streets in Seoul before pedestrian signals changed.Walking with his grandparents to places such as the local grocery shop and park helped him recognise the limitations of conventional crossing signals. The time allowed to cross did not always match the pace at which they could comfortably walk.That experience stayed with him, and eventually influenced how he approached technology. He began to wonder if a more responsive system might be a practical solution. His project exemplifies how a simple observation can lead to an idea that goes beyond the original problem.The main advantage of SmartBlink is its capacity to estimate the time a pedestrian needs to cross the road. Instead of following an unchanging schedule, the system can adapt the crossing period to the person's observed movement.If a pedestrian signal normally provides 20 seconds to cross, but the system estimates that a person needs 34 seconds, it can add another 14 seconds to the crossing period.This adjustment is intended to reduce the pressure pedestrians may feel when trying to reach the other side before the light changes. It also recognises that crossing a road can be more challenging for someone who walks slowly or uses a mobility aid.According to NiceNews, SmartBlink can identify pedestrians using wheelchairs, crutches or walking canes. Its algorithm has also been adapted to function under different lighting conditions, supporting its potential use during both daytime and night-time hours.A crossing that works well for one person may not provide enough time for another. SmartBlink seeks to address that difference by adapting the signal to the person crossing.Jung's work received recognition at the 2026 Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair, an international competition for secondary-school students presenting scientific and engineering projects.According to the Society for Science, Jung won 1st place in the Behavioral and Social Sciences category for SmartBlink. The project was recognised under the title ‘SmartBlink: Real-Time AI-Driven Adaptive Pedestrian Traffic System for Enhancing Perceived Pedestrian Safety and Traffic Efficiency.’The award came with a prize of $6,000. The recognition placed his project among a broad range of student-led research initiatives exploring practical problems through science and technology. In Jung's case, the focus was on making existing urban infrastructure more responsive to the people who depend on it.Despite the award, the system has not yet been installed at pedestrian crossings. Its next stage involves exploring how it could be tested in actual communities and adapted to local conditions.
Article Summary: Jay Jung, 18, of Massachusetts, developed the system called SmartBlink. Instead of a set time for crossing, it changes the pedestrian light timings based on how fast people cross the road. It aims to make streets more accessible to older adults and others with physical difficulties.

Article Title: US Immigration authorities return Indian national to Oregon jail over crash that killed newlywed couple
Article Text:
Indian national returned to US Oregon jail over crash that killed two newlyweds

US authorities have transferred 32-year-old Indian national Rajinder Kumar to state custody in Oregon to face prosecution over a November 2025 tractor-trailer crash that killed two newlywed Americans, the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said.Kumar has been indicted in Deschutes County, Oregon, on two counts of first-degree manslaughter and three counts of recklessly endangering another person. The charges remain pending before the state court, and the allegations have not been established at trial.In a post on X on Sunday, October 18, ICE's Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) Seattle office confirmed Kumar's transfer to the Deschutes County Jail, saying the move would allow state criminal proceedings to continue.“Two Americans lost their lives, and their families deserve accountability,” ICE ERO Seattle Acting Field Office Director Julio S Hernandez said, according to the agency's official statement.“ICE worked closely with law-enforcement partners to ensure Kumar is returned to state custody to answer for the serious charges against him,” Hernandez added, according to ANI.He further said, “This coordinated action protects the public, supports the victims’ families, and ensures that an individual accused of these crimes does not evade justice.”“ICE will continue using every lawful tool available to protect the American people from criminal activity committed by illegal aliens,” Hernandez said.According to ICE, the agency had lodged an immigration detainer with the Deschutes County Jail following Kumar's earlier arrest. However, the county released him in April 2026 without honouring the detainer, the agency said.“ICE officers subsequently located and arrested Kumar at large earlier this year,” the agency said in its post, without specifying the date or location of his subsequent arrest.ICE said deportation proceedings would remain on hold until the conclusion of the state criminal case. “Following the conclusion of state criminal proceedings, ICE will pursue Kumar’s immigration case consistent with federal law,” it said.The agency's statement also outlined Kumar's immigration history. According to ICE, US Border Patrol apprehended him near Lukeville, Arizona, on November 28, 2022, after he “illegally entered the United States from Mexico”.He was subsequently placed in removal proceedings. ICE said that “a pending application does not confer legal status in the United States”.
Article Summary: Rajinder Kumar, 32, has been indicted in Deschutes County, Oregon, on two counts of first-degree manslaughter and three counts of recklessly endangering another person. The charges remain pending before the state court, and the allegations have not been established at trial. According to ICE, US Border Patrol apprehended him near Lukeville, Arizona, on November 28, 2022.

Article Title: A 52-year-old Oregon farmer started building miniature castles from rocks cleared off his land in 1935, turning a winter hobby into a four-acre garden of stone bridges, churches and landmarks
Article Text:
AI Generated

How Danish immigrant began building Petersen Rock Garden at age 52

The stonework that put Petersen Rock Garden on the map

The miniature landmarks attract visitors

New owners took steps to restore the historic garden and museum

A historic attraction enters a new chapter

In central Oregon, a collection of ordinary stones became the raw material for an unusual roadside attraction. Rasmus Petersen, a Danish immigrant who had spent much of his life farming near Redmond, started arranging rocks into miniature buildings during the winter of 1935, according to Petersen Rock Garden, Museum and Peacock Sanctuary. He was 52, and what began as a seasonal pastime gradually spread across the land around his home. Small castles, churches, bridges and other structures took shape from stones gathered in the surrounding region, with ponds and planted areas added to the setting. The result became Petersen Rock Garden, a four-acre site that drew thousands of visitors during its early years and remains a recognised part of the area's history.Petersen arrived in Oregon in 1905, settling first in Junction City before claiming an 80-acre homestead near Redmond the following year. The land was acquired under the Desert Land Act, a federal scheme intended to encourage settlement and irrigation in arid parts of the American West. Farming became his livelihood, and by the 1920s he had expanded his agricultural holdings to 256 acres, growing hay and grain and keeping livestock.The Great Depression brought difficult conditions for farmers across the country. Petersen adapted by turning to potatoes, but it was away from the demands of agricultural work that he began developing a different kind of project. Reportedly, in 1935, at the age of 52, he started using the colder months to build small structures from rocks cleared from his land. What he made with them would eventually draw attention well beyond his immediate neighbours.The stones were not simply building material. Petersen incorporated local agate, jasper, obsidian and other varieties into his miniature constructions, selecting pieces for their shapes, colours and textures. Bridges linked sections of the garden, while castles, churches and monuments gave the site the appearance of a small settlement assembled from the geology of the region.The work grew over time. Water features, fountains, mosses and flowers became part of the surroundings, adding living elements to the carefully arranged stonework. Petersen also collected stones from within roughly 85 miles of his home, according to the garden's historical account. That broad geographical reach meant the site reflected the variety of material found across central Oregon rather than relying entirely on rocks from a single field.Visitors began arriving while the garden was still developing. By 1938, the attraction had reportedly welcomed more than 7,000 people. What had started as something to occupy the winter months was becoming a destination in its own right.Petersen Rock Garden eventually covered four acres, with its stone creations arranged among landscaped areas and water. Its appeal lay partly in the contrast between the scale of the structures and the work required to assemble them. Buildings and bridges were made from individual stones, placed together to suggest larger architectural forms in miniature.The site also expanded beyond the garden itself. Historical accounts describe a museum, a diner and a pond with islands among its features. Reportedly, by the early 1950s, annual attendance was said to have reached around 120,000 visitors, placing the garden among the roadside attractions that drew travellers exploring Oregon.One plaque on the property sits beneath a miniature Statue of Liberty. It carries the inscription, “Enjoy yourself. It is later than you think.” The wording offers a small glimpse into the garden's character, although its buildings and collections remain the more substantial record of Petersen's years of work.Petersen devoted himself to the project until his death in 1952. His wife, Nyleta Harris, whom he had married in 1950, continued managing the property until she died in 1987. The garden then passed into the care of her daughter, Adele Hegardt, and her husband, Harry. Following Adele's death, her daughter Susan Caward took on responsibility for the site.The stone structures, planted areas and water features all formed part of a landscape that had developed over decades, rather than a conventional museum collection that could be preserved indoors. In 2010, an Oregon family purchased the site, with preservation efforts organised through a nonprofit established to support the garden, museum and peacock sanctuary. The aim was to protect the attraction and restore features associated with its earlier years. A museum refurbishment followed in 2022 after a grant secured through local business Webfoot Home Improvements.More recent efforts have focused on bringing people back into the work of caring for the garden. Since 2022, Marci Wayman has been associated with new ownership and plans to develop the landmark as a community-stewarded nonprofit. Volunteers have helped with restoration and upkeep, while organisers have sought wider participation in deciding how the property should be preserved and used.The garden's future now depends on more than the stonework Petersen left behind. Its museum, landscape and other features need attention if they are to remain accessible, and community involvement has become part of that process. The original structures still connect the site to the farmer who began building them in 1935, long before the garden became a familiar stop for visitors travelling through central Oregon.
Article Summary: Danish immigrant Rasmus Petersen began building Petersen Rock Garden in 1935. The four-acre site drew thousands of visitors during its early years. New owners have taken steps to restore the historic garden and museum. The future of the site depends more on the stonework left behind than how it is preserved.

Article Title: Randy Orton paid a viral WWE impersonator's $2,400 wrestling school tuition, Zy reveals on Instagram
Article Text:
Image: Left/Wikipedia/Right/Zy/Wrestlelamia/Instagram

Who is Zy: The viral online creator behind the ‘Be Like’ videos imitating professional wrestling legends

Image: WWE

Randy Orton paid $2,400 in full: Zy announced the wrestling school tuition on Instagram stories

Why Randy Orton's gesture resonates with fans, a legend nicknamed The Viper backs an aspiring wrestler

From basketball impressions to the ring, Zy shares training videos from Test Of Strength Wrestling

Zy's wrestling school journey and Randy Orton's SmackDown face-to-face with Cody Rhodes

Sometimes generosity arrives from the most unexpected corner of the ring. A creator known online as Zy built a following by imitating professional wrestlers in viral videos, while working toward becoming a wrestler himself. Then came a surprise from one of the sport's biggest names. Randy Orton , nicknamed The Viper, reportedly covered his full wrestling school tuition of $2,400. The creator shared the news on Instagram, saying he had been wondering how he would pay. Read on to discover who Zy is, what he said, how his videos caught on, and why this act of kindness resonates with wrestling fans.Zy, whom eWrestling identifies as T'Zaih, has built an audience through a series of videos known as Be Like. In them, he imitates professional wrestlers. eWrestling lists Randy Orton, Batista, The Boogeyman, Zack Ryder, Triple H, and Roman Reigns among the stars he has mimicked, while Fightful adds Kurt Angle, Booker T, and Rob Van Dam, and notes that he has even recreated match types such as ladder matches. Both outlets describe him as a viral star, a label that reflects how widely his clips have circulated. Fightful also reports that before wrestling videos, he made basketball videos imitating well-known players.Imitation videos like these work because they reward close knowledge of each performer's mannerisms, which suggests a genuine fan's understanding of the business.The news came directly from Zy. According to eWrestling, he shared on his Instagram stories that Randy Orton covered the cost of his professional wrestling school tuition, a total of $2,400. Fightful's report, published a day earlier on 11 October 2026, says the same, Orton paid $2,400, which helped Zy cover his wrestling school. Zy told his followers, in a message eWrestling reproduced, "The Legend Killer just paid for my wrestling school tuition!" He added that he had been wondering how he was going to afford it. Notably, The Legend Killer is one of Orton's long-standing nicknames, and Zy's choice to use it reads as an affectionate nod from a fan who has imitated Orton himself. The amount is modest by the standards of professional sport, yet for a trainee it can be the difference between starting and waiting.Wrestling fans and outlets responded warmly. Fightful embedded a post from the account Wrestlelamia.com, which told its followers on X that Randy Orton "is a beautiful soul" and paid the full wrestling tuition fee of $2,400. Both news outlets frame the gesture as generosity: Fightful opens its report by saying Orton gives back, while eWrestling describes him as a legend who generously covered the cost. Orton, nicknamed The Viper, carries enormous recognition among wrestling audiences, which makes the gesture especially striking for a trainee hoping to follow in the footsteps of the very performers he imitates. For Zy, the support probably means more than money alone; it signals that a performer he has spent time studying and recreating has noticed his effort and wanted to help him continue.Zy is not only imitating wrestlers; he is training to become one. Fightful reports that, alongside replicating legends in the business, he is preparing for a wrestling career himself, and that before wrestling content he made viral basketball videos imitating well-known players. eWrestling adds that he has posted training videos from the ring on social media, including sessions at Test Of Strength Wrestling. Those clips matter because they let followers watch his progress over time, turning an imitation persona into a visible apprenticeship. Wrestling schools typically teach fundamentals such as falling safely, working with a partner, and building matches, which is why tuition can be a significant barrier for hopeful performers. Fightful closed its report by wishing Zy the best of luck on his wrestling journey.The story also arrived during a busy week for Orton. According to eWrestling, that week's episode of World Wrestling Entertainment ( WWE ) SmackDown was set to feature a face-to-face confrontation between Orton and his rival Cody Rhodes, whom eWrestling calls The American Nightmare. It is a reminder that even while preparing for a major storyline, Orton took time for a gesture of support off-screen. For Zy, the next step is straightforward but demanding to continue his wrestling school training and keep documenting the journey online. For readers, the story offers a simple lesson, kindness often works quietly, and a single act of support can change what feels possible for someone chasing a dream. Both Fightful and eWrestling published the news within a day of the Instagram announcement.
Article Summary: Randy Orton, nicknamed The Viper, reportedly covered the full wrestling school tuition of Zy. Zy is the creator of the 'Be Like' videos imitating professional wrestling legends. He is not only imitating wrestlers, but he is also training to become one himself.

Article Title: Pakistan army officer killed in IED blast during Balochistan operation
Article Text:
Pakistan Army major killed in Balochistan IED blast as security forces eliminate four terrorists.

A Pakistan Army major was killed in an improvised explosive device (IED) blast during a security operation in Balochistan province, while security forces killed four terrorists in a separate operation, the military said on Monday.According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the military's media wing, security forces conducted operations in the Shadi Kaur area of Gwadar and Jattakabad in Kalat district on Sunday following reports of terrorist presence.During an operation in Jattakabad, the forces killed four terrorists and recovered “a large cache of arms and ammunition”, the Army said.In a separate action, security forces carried out clearance operations in the Shadi Kaur area of Pasni in Gwadar district. During the operation, 34-year-old Major Wajahat Waheed was killed in an IED attack while leading the operation.“Sanitisation operations will continue to eliminate any other terrorists found in the area,” the Army said.The military added that security forces and law enforcement agencies remained committed to eliminating foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism in the country.Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to the security forces for killing the four terrorists and expressed grief over the death of the officer.“Major Wajahat Waheed sacrificed his life for the protection of our beloved homeland; the nation is proud of its brave son,” the prime minister said.Sharif also extended condolences to the officer's family and prayed for the elevation of his rank.Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years, with security forces continuing operations to contain the violence.A day earlier, security forces killed eight terrorists during operations in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts.(With inputs from PTI)
Article Summary: Pakistan Army major killed in Balochistan IED blast as security forces eliminate four terrorists. Major Wajahat Waheed was killed in an IED attack while leading the operation. Security forces carried out clearance operations in the Shadi Kaur area of Pasni in Gwadar district.

Article Title: US-designated LeT terrorist dies after mysteriously falling from building in Lahore
Article Text:
LeT terrorist Chaudhary Muhammed Sarwar.

NEW DELHI: US designated Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Chaudhry Mohammad Sarwar alias Abu Hashim, one of the founding members of the outfit, died after mysteriously falling from the fourth floor of Markaz Qudesia in Lahore Sunday.The incident reminded of a similar death that had occurred in 2016 when fake currency kingpin, Javed Khanani, had died after falling from an under construction building in Karachi.Sarwar was currently handling the finance wing and fundraising excercise in Punjab province under the garb of the outfit's political wing, Pakistan Markazi Muslim League. He was a close aide of both Hafiz Saeed and current deputy chief Saifullah Kasuri. Sarwar's son had also died in a road accident a few months ago.It was in 2016 tha Sarwar was designated a terrorist by the US justice department who termed himself as a senior LeT memeber in Lahore active since early 2000s, holding various leadership roles in the group. At the time, he was LeT’s emir for Lahore, a position he has held since at least January 2015."As the LeT emir of Lahore, Sarwar maintains relationships with LeT’s most senior leaders. Between 2012 and 2013, Sarwar worked with LeT’s foreign affairs chief Hafiz Abdul Rahman Makki, and in early 2013, Makki asked Sarwar for money to pay for his travel within Pakistan," the US justice department had said in its statement."Sarwar had been directly involved in LeT fundraising activities and used the formal financial system in Pakistan to raise and move funds on behalf of LeT. For example, in 2008, Sarwar led delegations of businessmen to LeT facilities for the purpose of soliciting donations for the group," it added.
Article Summary: US designated Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Chaudhry Mohammad Sarwar alias Abu Hashim died after mysteriously falling from the fourth floor of Markaz Qudesia in Lahore Sunday. Sarwar was currently handling the finance wing and fundraising excercise in Punjab province under the garb of the outfit's political wing, Pakistan Markazi Muslim League.

Article Title: Pakistani forces kill 8 militants in Balochistan, raid hideouts as abductions rise
Article Text:
The operations took place on Saturday in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts, following intelligence that the militants were hiding in those areas (Photo: ANI).

Pakistani security forces on Sunday reportedly killed eight militants in three intelligence-led operations across districts of Balochistan province, amid rising cases of abduction in the troubled region.The operations took place on Saturday in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts, following intelligence that the militants were hiding in those areas, according to the Inter Service Public Relations (ISPR), the media wing of the Pakistan Army.In the Panjpai area of Quetta district, terrorists trying to set up a roadblock to disrupt local traffic were "intercepted by security forces, resulting in [the] killing of five terrorists", the ISPR said in a statement.In Nushki district, security forces stormed a hideout, and two terrorists were killed in an intense exchange of fire, the army said. Around 500 kilograms of explosives were also recovered from the terrorists during that operation. In Khuzdar district, one terrorist was killed, the ISPR added.Balochistan, which borders Afghanistan, has seen a surge in abductions and attacks on civilians and securityforces in recent years, prompting the government to step up its anti-militant operations.On Saturday, unidentified armed men hijacked a bus carrying 20 trainee police officers near Mastung, on the Quetta-Karachi highway, and took them away. Their whereabouts remain unknown.On Sunday, at least 18 workers were abducted, and another was injured when unidentified armed men attacked a marble mining site in the province. The incident happened early in the morning in the remote Naal area of Khuzdar district, police said. The attackers arrived on motorcycles and other vehicles and stormed the site.According to PTI, no insurgent group or individual has claimed responsibility for the attack.The police and the provincial government have yet to confirm the incident officially, but two police officers, speaking on condition of anonymity, said 18 workers had been taken away by the attackers. PTI reported."They came on bikes and vehicles and opened fire and then rounded up the workers present at the site and abducted 18 of them before fleeing," a police officer said.Most of those abducted came from nearby villages and areas, he added, and another worker was injured in the attack.
Article Summary: Pakistani security forces reportedly kill eight militants in three intelligence- led operations across districts of Balochistan province. Operations took place on Saturday in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts, following intelligence that the militants were hiding in those areas. On Saturday, unidentified armed men hijacked a bus carrying 20 trainee police officers.

Article Title: Pakistan’s decades of backing terror comes full circle as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa falls under emergency rule
Article Text:
The emergency has also raised concerns about the separation of powers. In the affected districts, the constitutional distinction between judicial and executive authority has reportedly been set aside, concentrating control in unelected hands.

Decades of militant policy and blowback

Emergency rule and the erosion of elected authority

Opposition crackdown deepens rights concerns

Tribal communities face renewed uncertainty

Pakistan’s imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11 has placed the province under direct federal control, effectively suspending the regional administration led by imprisoned former prime minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).The move, which invokes Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, comes amid a worsening security situation and a crackdown on opposition leaders and protesters. It has also renewed questions over Pakistan’s decades-long policy of using militant groups for strategic gains, which critics say has fuelled the violence now threatening its own territory.The emergency has extended federal control across 12 districts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, further weakening elected authority in a province that has long borne the consequences of Pakistan’s security policies. The move follows years of political turmoil, including Khan’s imprisonment, constitutional amendments that have weakened judicial independence, and the removal of the PTI-led provincial government.The concentration of power in unelected authorities, alongside the military’s expanding role in civilian affairs, has raised concerns over the state of democracy in Pakistan, according to a report by news agency ANI.Pakistan’s security crisis has deep roots in its long-standing use of militant groups as instruments of state policy. For more than five decades, the country has pursued strategic depth through its relationship with armed groups, while distinguishing between factions considered useful and those viewed as threats.This approach has contributed to a cycle of violence that has increasingly turned inward. The state has repeatedly shifted its position towards militant organisations, including groups hostile to its own security forces. During former army chief General Qamar Javed Bajwa’s tenure, cadres of the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) were relocated to parts of the erstwhile Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.The consequences have proved difficult to contain. Pakistan’s struggle with militancy has exposed the risks of treating armed groups as strategic assets while assuming their violence can be directed towards selected targets.Former US secretary of state Hillary Clinton captured this danger in a widely cited remark: “one cannot rear snakes in a backyard and expect them to bite only neighbours, as they will eventually turn on their keepers”.Rather than confronting the broader implications of this policy, Pakistan has continued to differentiate between militant factions it considers acceptable and those it seeks to eliminate. The resulting security failures have placed civilians, particularly in the tribal areas, at the centre of a prolonged conflict.The imposition of emergency rule marks another stage in the concentration of power within Pakistan’s security establishment. The federal intervention has effectively displaced the PTI-led provincial administration, depriving the opposition of its remaining provincial government.The move follows Khan’s incarceration and constitutional changes that have curtailed judicial independence and shielded military leadership from accountability. Critics argue that these developments have weakened the institutions meant to limit executive and military power.The emergency has also raised concerns about the separation of powers. In the affected districts, the constitutional distinction between judicial and executive authority has reportedly been set aside, concentrating control in unelected hands.Instead of addressing the failures behind the province’s deteriorating security situation, authorities have expanded federal and military involvement in civilian administration. The move has intensified concerns that emergency powers are being used not only to manage the security crisis but also to consolidate political control.The intervention has been accompanied by a wider crackdown on the opposition. Leaders and legislators have been detained, residences raided and political demonstrations suppressed. Protesters have faced police firing, tear gas and mass arrests.The treatment of political opponents has fuelled concerns that dissent is increasingly being treated as a security threat. The use of force against protesters has also raised questions about the government’s claim that extraordinary measures are needed to restore law and order.The crackdown comes amid concerns over restrictions on reporting from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, following earlier developments in Khyber before a blanket media ban was imposed on events in the province. Such restrictions risk limiting public scrutiny of security operations and their impact on civilians.The growing concentration of authority has therefore created a parallel crisis. While the state faces a persistent militant threat, its response has further narrowed the space for political opposition and public dissent.The latest intervention has also placed additional pressure on communities that have endured years of displacement and insecurity. Past military operations, including Zarb-e-Azb and Radd-ul-Fasad, remain associated with civilian hardship and human rights concerns.Thousands of displaced families are still awaiting return and rehabilitation. For these communities, the emergency raises fears of another period of disruption, particularly as the authorities expand their control and military involvement in civilian affairs.The consequences of Pakistan’s security policies have thus extended beyond the fight against armed groups. Tribal populations have faced displacement, civilian casualties and prolonged instability, while the failure to resolve the underlying conflict has left many vulnerable to further intervention.The emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa brings these tensions into sharper focus. A state that has long relied on militant groups to pursue strategic objectives now faces the consequences of violence within its own borders. Its response, however, has centred on expanding federal control, weakening elected authority and restricting opposition activity.Rather than resolving the crisis, the latest measures risk deepening the divide between the state and the communities it claims to protect. The removal of an elected provincial government, the concentration of power in unelected institutions and the crackdown on dissent point to a broader struggle over Pakistan’s democratic future, even as the country confronts the long-term fallout of its militant policies.
Article Summary: The emergency has extended federal control across 12 districts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The move comes amid a worsening security situation and a crackdown on opposition leaders and protesters. It has also renewed questions over Pakistan’s decades-long policy of using militant groups for strategic gains.

Article Title: Pakistan plans Moon landing by 2035, expands space cooperation with China
Article Text:
Pakistan sets 2035 Moon landing target as space programme expands, minister says (representative image)

First Pakistani astronaut to travel to China’s space station

Pakistan-China cooperation extends to lunar exploration

Space education and proposed museum

India’s space roadmap: From Gaganyaan to a Moon landing

Pakistan aims to land on the Moon by 2035 as it expands its space programme, planning minister Ahsan Iqbal said on Sunday, announcing that the country's first astronaut would embark on a space mission from China on November 25.Addressing the concluding ceremony of World Space Week 2026 in Narowal district of Punjab province, Iqbal said cooperation with China would help Pakistan advance its space exploration ambitions.Pakistan’s “first astronaut will embark on a space mission from China’s space centre on November 25, while the country aims to achieve a lunar landing by 2035,” he said, according to news agency PTI.The minister highlighted the growing role of space technology in agriculture, communications, climate monitoring, education and national security. He stressed that scientific research and space exploration were important for technological advancement.The upcoming mission is part of wider cooperation between Pakistan and China in space science and technology. According to Reuters, two Pakistani candidates, pilots Khurram Daud and Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, have been undergoing training in China, with one expected to be selected for the flight.The selected astronaut will serve as a payload specialist aboard China's Tiangong space station, conducting scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft, Reuters reported last month.Pakistan's space agency, the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO), signed an agreement with the China Manned Space Agency in February 2025 to prepare a Pakistani astronaut for the mission, according to The Express Tribune.The two candidates had been training at the China Astronaut Research and Training Centre in Beijing, learning spacecraft systems, Mandarin and the physical demands of spaceflight.The mission is expected to last about a week. The astronaut will travel aboard a Chinese spacecraft launched from China and return to Earth with members of a Chinese crew.Pakistan does not have an independent launch vehicle or crewed spacecraft, making the mission dependent on China's space infrastructure and training facilities.Beyond the human spaceflight programme, Pakistan and China are collaborating on a Pakistani-built lunar rover planned for China's Chang'e-8 mission, expected around 2028.The rover is intended to use artificial intelligence-based stereo imaging to identify obstacles, assess distances and navigate the lunar surface autonomously, as direct real-time control from Earth would not be possible.However, Pakistan's participation in the lunar rover project is separate from its stated ambition to land on the Moon by 2035.According to Reuters, a Pakistani space agency official last month had said there was no official commitment or discussion about sending a Pakistani astronaut to the Moon under the existing partnership.Iqbal was speaking at the conclusion of World Space Week 2026, which was celebrated in Narowal for the first time in collaboration with SUPARCO. The event aimed to raise awareness among young people about space science, scientific research and modern technology.The minister also announced plans to establish Pakistan's first Space Museum at the University of Narowal to promote scientific awareness and encourage students to pursue careers in space science and technology.He said improved access to higher education was allowing students who had previously faced financial barriers to perform well academically.Iqbal congratulated the University of Narowal on securing first position at the Islamabad Science Festival, saying the achievement reflected the talent and potential of Pakistan's youth.The minister said the proposed museum would further encourage young people to explore scientific fields and pursue opportunities in space research and technology.India has also been advancing its space programme, with plans to send astronauts into orbit, establish its own space station and land an Indian on the Moon by 2040.According to the Union government’s roadmap outlined in Parliament in August, the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission, carrying the humanoid robot Vyommitra, is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026. Two further uncrewed missions are planned before India attempts its first crewed orbital flight, targeted by 2027.India also plans to establish the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035. The proposed station will comprise five modules, with the development and launch of its first module already approved.The longer-term goal is to send an Indian astronaut to the Moon by 2040.Other planned missions include Chandrayaan-4, which is intended to demonstrate technologies for returning lunar samples to Earth, and a Venus Orbiter Mission to study the planet’s surface, subsurface and atmosphere.These projects form part of India’s broader Space Vision 2047, which aims to expand its human spaceflight capabilities and deepen its role in space exploration.
Article Summary: Pakistan's first astronaut will embark on a space mission from China on November 25. Ahsan Iqbal said cooperation with China would help Pakistan advance its space exploration ambitions. Pakistan and China are collaborating on a Pakistani-built lunar rover planned for China's Chang'e-8 mission, expected around 2028.

Article Title: Balochistan unrest: Teacher's killing sparks outrage, kin say Pak officials shielding 'death squads'
Article Text:
What are Balochistan's 'death squads'?

(With ANI inputs)

The alleged torture and killing of a teacher in Pakistan’s restive Balochistan province triggered protests by his family members and local residents, who warned that a key highway would be blockaded if authorities failed to take action.The protesters accused Pakistani forces of shielding those allegedly responsible for the death of Parvez Mazar, an Arabic teacher at Government High School Babbar Shor in Pasni, a coastal town in Balochistan’s Gwadar district, The Balochistan Post reported.According to Mazar’s relatives, he was "taken away" in front of his family on Tuesday and was found dead the following day. They claimed that members of a state-backed armed group, described as a “death squad,” took him to a private torture facility, where he was detained and killed.Protesters, including Mazar’s children, gathered outside the Pasni Press Club, demanding the immediate arrest of those responsible for his death. They demanded accountability and justice for the deceased teacher's family.The demonstrators warned that failure to address their demands would prompt them to stage a sit-in at Pasni Zero Point and block the Makran Coastal Highway, a key route connecting Gwadar with Karachi in Sindh province, Pakistan’s largest city and the country's financial and commercial hub.They demanded that state institutions take action against armed groups accused of abducting, torturing and killing civilians while allegedly operating under the protection of state agencies.Baloch rights organisations and activists use the term “death squads” to describe armed groups they allege receive support or protection from Pakistani state institutions.These groups have been accused of targeting civilians, political activists and human rights defenders in Balochistan, a province long affected by an insurgency and a security crackdown.
Article Summary: Pervez Mazar, an Arabic teacher at Government High School Babbar Shor in Pasni, a coastal town in Balochistan’s Gwadar district, was found dead the following day. His family claimed that members of a state-backed armed group, described as a “death squad,” took him to a private torture facility, where he was detained and killed.

Article Title: Strong 6.0-magnitude quake strikes Balochistan in Pakistan
Article Text:
6.0-magnitude quake strikes Balochistan in Pakistan

More details awaited

An earthquake measuring 6.0 in magnitude struck southern Pakistan near Khuzdar, Balochistan on Saturday, around 95 km south of Sūrāb, according to the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC).The German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) said the earthquake struck at a depth of 10 km (6 miles).
Article Summary: An earthquake measuring 6.0 in magnitude struck southern Pakistan near Khuzdar, Balochistan on Saturday. The German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) said the earthquake struck at a depth of 10 km (6 miles)

Article Title: Imran Khan facing Nawaz, Benazir-style exile deal? Pakistan opposition leader's big claim
Article Text:
Imran Khan

What happened in Nawaz Sharif, Benazir Bhutto's exile cases?

Achakzai demands access to prisoners, empowered parliament

Opposition challenges governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

Pakistan opposition leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai has claimed that jailed former prime minister Imran Khan is being pressured into an agreement similar to arrangements that led former premiers Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto into exile, according to a report by Dawn published on Saturday.Achakzai, chairman of the Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP) and leader of the opposition in Pakistan's National Assembly, made the claim at a news conference at the Peshawar high court on Friday. He alleged that the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) were involved in a similar political arrangement.“The same is happening today with the PML-N and PPP in government,” Achakzai said, according to Dawn.The claim comes amid political tensions surrounding Imran Khan, founder of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), who remains in prison, and opposition allegations over restrictions on political activity and the functioning of elected institutions.Achakzai was accompanied by Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) leaders Sardar Akhtar Mengal and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas. He said opposition parties were in contact and that a multi-party conference would be convened soon.He also said resigning from the assemblies remained an option, adding that the opposition had submitted its demands in response to an offer of negotiations.Achakzai's remarks referred to the circumstances in which Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto, two of Pakistan's most prominent former prime ministers, spent periods outside the country following political upheavals, Dawnreported.Sharif was ousted and imprisoned after a military coup led by then-army chief Pervez Musharraf. He left Pakistan in 2000 under a deal negotiated with the involvement of Saudi and Lebanese leaders.Bhutto, meanwhile, went into self-imposed exile after her Pakistan Peoples Party lost the 1997 general elections, following her dismissal by then-president Farooq Leghari. Her husband, Asif Ali Zardari, was imprisoned on corruption charges and was released in 2004.Achakzai's comparison suggests that he believes a similar arrangement could be pursued in Khan's case. However, his remarks, as reported by Dawn, did not establish that an exile agreement involving the PTI founder had been reached.During the news conference, Achakzai criticised restrictions on prisoners' access to meetings and called for changes to what he described as a "wrong amendment". He also demanded that parliament be empowered and an independent commission be established to ensure transparent elections.“Nowhere in the world is a prisoner denied meetings,” he said, according to Dawn.He argued that political disputes could not be resolved without strengthening parliament. He also expressed concern over the whereabouts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's chief minister and other lawmakers, demanding that the authorities disclose the chief minister's location.“We stand with the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The people of this province have the first right over its minerals. Regardless of political affiliation, everyone must unite for the homeland,” he said, adding that they would be safer if the country survived.Mengal, who accompanied Achakzai, criticised the government's actions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and questioned the imposition of governor's rule on grounds of terrorism. He also alleged that elected representatives had been displaced and questioned the legitimacy of the political system.Raja Nasir Abbas, the opposition leader in the Senate, also criticised the situation, saying: “You cannot run a country, yet you have occupied a province,” according to Dawn.Separately, TTAP leaders approached the Peshawar High Court on Friday, challenging the proclamation of emergency and the imposition of governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.According to Dawn, the petitioners asked the court to declare the October 11 proclamation, issued under Articles 232(1) and 234 of Pakistan's Constitution, unconstitutional and without lawful authority. They argued that the constitutional conditions required for imposing the measures had not been met or that the government had exceeded its powers.The petition also challenged the purported transfer of the provincial assembly's legislative powers to parliament, the displacement of the elected chief minister and provincial cabinet, and the establishment of the proposed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Advisory Council and Area Development Secretariat.The petitioners sought the annulment of executive orders and notifications linked to the proclamation, including the deployment of armed forces to the extent that it allegedly violated constitutional requirements.They also requested interim relief to prevent the displacement of elected institutions and restrictions on elected representatives while the court considers the case.The legal challenge adds to the opposition's broader campaign against federal intervention in the province, as Achakzai seeks to bring opposition parties together over constitutional issues, political rights and negotiations with the government.
Article Summary: Mahmood Khan Achakzai claims Imran Khan is being pressured into an agreement similar to those that led Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto into exile. He claims the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) are involved in a similar political arrangement. The opposition leader made the claim at a news conference at the Peshawar high court on Friday.

Article Title: Pakistan to chair IMF, World Bank boards in 2027; first time in over 70 years
Article Text:
The announcement was made during the plenary session of the 2026 WBG-IMF annual meetings in Bangkok (Photo: AP).

Pakistan will take over the chairmanship of the boards of governors of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group in 2027, returning to the position for the first time since 1953, the country’s ministry of economic affairs said on Friday.The announcement was made during the plenary session of the 2026 WBG-IMF annual meetings in Bangkok, where Pakistan’s minister for economic affairs Ahad Khan Cheema, who also serves as the country’s governor to the World Bank, was formally designated as the incoming chair, PTI reported.Describing the appointment as a “historic milestone”, the ministry said the role would allow Pakistan to participate in shaping global economic and development discussions and encourage constructive engagement among member countries.The annual meetings, scheduled from October 12 to 18, have brought together more than 15,000 participants representing 191 countries.The appointment comes as Pakistan continues to rely on financial assistance from the IMF through two programmes: a USD 7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and a USD 1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).While the EFF is aimed at meeting the country’s balance-of-payments needs and supporting economic reforms, the RSF provides longer-term funding to help Pakistan tackle climate-related risks and improve its resilience.Pakistan could receive a further USD 1.2 billion from the IMF, subject to approval by the fund’s Executive Board. The anticipated disbursement follows an agreement reached between IMF staff and Pakistani authorities on the latest reviews of both programmes.
Article Summary: Pakistan will take over the chairmanship of the boards of governors of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group in 2027. The announcement was made during the plenary session of the 2026 WBG-IMF annual meetings in Bangkok. Pakistan continues to rely on financial assistance from the IMF through two programmes.

Article Title: Pakistan ranks lowest in South Asia on hunger index amid rising food prices
Article Text:
Pakistan's 2026 Global Hunger Index standings reveal an alarming crisis, showcasing the worst performance in South Asia amid ongoing economic challenges. (Pic Credit: ANI)

Economic crisis and food inflation worsen Pakistan’s hunger situation

Hunger reduction stalls across South Asia

Extreme weather threatens regional food production

Millions across South Asia continue to face undernourishment

Pakistan has recorded the poorest performance in South Asia in the 2026 global hunger index (GHI), reflecting mounting food insecurity driven by economic instability, rising food prices, climate-related disasters and international conflicts, according to a report by Dawn.Titled “No Security Without Food Security”, the report was jointly prepared by German aid organisation Welthungerhilfe, the institute for international law of peace and armed conflict at Ruhr university Bochum, and swiss organisation helvetas.According to the news agency ANI, the findings indicate that progress in reducing hunger across South Asia has largely stagnated, while Pakistan and Afghanistan have experienced a deterioration in conditions since 2018.Pakistan’s economic challenges and persistent food inflation have eroded household purchasing power, making it increasingly difficult for families to access sufficient and nutritious food.The report noted that Pakistan’s undernourishment indicator had deteriorated from a low level in 2018 to a medium level. Meanwhile, child wasting has approached the threshold associated with the high category, underscoring continuing concerns over child nutrition.South Asia recorded an overall global hunger index score of 23.5, placing the region in the serious category. While the score represents an improvement from 37.5 in 2000, the report suggests that much of the progress was achieved before 2018.Over the past two decades, Pakistan and Afghanistan have moved out of the alarming hunger category. However, persistent levels of child malnutrition continue to pose a significant challenge in both countries.Child stunting has continued to decline in Pakistan, while Afghanistan has recorded a slight increase in the indicator since 2018.Child mortality rates have improved in both countries, falling from very high levels in 2000 to medium levels in the latest assessment.The report also drew attention to the growing impact of extreme weather events on agricultural production and food security across South Asia.Heavy rainfall and flooding damaged crops in parts of Pakistan and Bangladesh. In Afghanistan, inadequate rainfall and unusually high temperatures disrupted the cereal-growing season in 2026.These climate-related pressures could further aggravate food shortages and prolong acute food insecurity across the region, according to Dawn.Estimates from the food and agriculture organisation (FAO) indicate that approximately 218 million people across South Asia, including Iran, experienced undernourishment between 2023 and 2025.This represents roughly one-third of the global population affected by undernourishment during the period, highlighting the scale of the region’s food security challenge.The findings underscore the need for sustained efforts to address economic vulnerabilities, improve access to nutritious food and strengthen agricultural resilience against climate-related shocks.
Article Summary: Pakistan has recorded the poorest performance in South Asia in the 2026 global hunger index (GHI) The report was prepared by German aid organisation Welthungerhilfe, the institute for international law of peace and armed conflict at Ruhr university Bochum, and swiss organisation helvetas. The findings indicate that progress in reducing hunger across South Asia has largely stagnated.

Article Title: 33 children, teacher killed as school roof collapses in Pakistan’s Peshawar
Article Text:
18 killed as school roof collapses in Pakistan's Peshawar

At least 33 students and a teacher were killed after the roof of a school collapsed in Pakistan 's Peshawar city on Thursday.Twenty students and a female teacher were killed and more than 40 people injured in the incident, officials said.Peshawar Capital City Police chief Mian Saeed said the incident occurred in Dir Colony in the city's inner area, as cited by PTI.Lady Reading Hospital spokesperson Muhammad Asim said an emergency had been declared at the facility to treat the injured.All the children killed in the incident were aged 13 or younger, Asim said. Rescue officials said 25 injured children had been taken to medical facilities.Rescue teams were clearing the debris and searching for children and school staff who might still be trapped beneath the collapsed structure.Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed deep grief over the loss of life and extended his condolences to the bereaved families.Building and roof collapses are common in Pakistan, largely due to poor safety standards and the use of substandard construction materials.In July, three girls aged between three and 13 were killed when part of the outer wall of a government primary school near Umerkot collapsed, burying them under the debris, as cited by Dawn.That same month, a child was killed and at least five others were injured when the roof of an under-construction private school building collapsed in Lahore’s Baghbanpura neighbourhood.In June, 14 children died after the roof of a private tuition centre collapsed in Lahore’s Kahna area. Less than two months earlier, four children were killed and 20 people injured when a classroom roof collapsed at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan.
Article Summary: Twenty students and a female teacher were killed and more than 40 people injured in the incident. The incident occurred in Dir Colony in the city's inner area. Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed deep grief over the loss of life and extended his condolences to the bereaved families.

Article Title: Pakistan regulator warns TV channels against live coverage of blasts and terror attacks
Article Text:
The regulator also stressed the need for stronger editorial oversight.

Channels told to air only verified information

Legal action for violations

Pakistan's media regulator has warned satellite television channels against broadcasting live footage of explosions, gunfire and terrorist attacks, cautioning that violations could lead to legal action.The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) issued a notification on Tuesday, reminding broadcasters of restrictions first introduced on February 20, 2023. The rules bar news, current affairs and regional-language channels from broadcasting, rebroadcasting or providing live coverage of such incidents.The directive comes as emergency rule has been imposed in the north-western province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, renewing debate over how the media should report security incidents while ensuring that the public receives timely and reliable information.PEMRA has instructed broadcasters to air only “verified information warranted by the relevant government departments or law enforcement agencies”.The regulator also stressed the need for stronger editorial oversight and the effective use of broadcast delays to prevent the immediate transmission of sensitive footage during security incidents.It directed television channels to establish independent editorial boards in line with applicable laws and relevant court judgments.The notification referred to the Supreme Court's judgment in Suo Motu Case No. 28 of 2018 and an Islamabad High Court order dated September 5, 2022, both concerning the prescribed procedure for broadcast delays.PEMRA warned that channels violating the directive could face legal proceedings under Sections 29A, 30 and 33 of the PEMRA Ordinance, 2002, as amended.The latest notification reiterates the regulator's existing restrictions on live coverage of security incidents, with a focus on verification, editorial checks and the use of broadcast delays.
Article Summary: Pakistan's media regulator has warned satellite television channels against broadcasting live footage of explosions, gunfire and terrorist attacks. The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) issued a notification on Tuesday. The rules bar news, current affairs and regional-language channels from broadcasting or providing live coverage of such incidents.

Article Title: 6 killed, several injured as passenger train derails in Pakistan's Punjab
Article Text:
Train travelling from Karachi to Peshawar derails in Pakistan (Representative image) (PTI)

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the top priority to prevent train accidents? Improving railway tracks Upgrading safety systems Regular maintenance and inspections 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

At least six people were killed and several others injured after a passenger train derailed in Pakistan's Punjab province early Tuesday, Pakistan-based Geo News reported.The Rehman Baba Express, travelling from the southern port city of Karachi to the northwestern city of Peshawar, derailed in Sher Shah, Punjab province, news agency AP reported, citing Pakistan Railways spokesperson Kaleem Akhtar.The injured were taken to Nishtar Hospital in Multan for treatment, while rescue teams continued operations at the accident site.The accident took place at around 5.15am, according to Geo News.Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed grief over the deaths in separate statements and directed authorities to ensure the best possible medical care for the injured.Train accidents are relatively common in Pakistan, where the railway system has suffered from decades of underinvestment, outdated tracks and ageing signalling systems.In 2023, 10 carriages of a passenger train derailed in southern Pakistan, killing 30 people and injuring more than 90 others.
Article Summary: Passenger train travelling from Karachi to Peshawar derails in Pakistan. At least six people killed and several others injured in Sher Shah, Punjab province. Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif express grief over the deaths.

Article Title: 2 Pakistan army pilots killed as training aircraft crashes near Balochistan's Quetta
Article Text:
2 Pakistan army pilots killed (IANS photo)

Two Pakistan army pilots were killed after a Mushshak training aircraft crashed near Balochistan's Quetta on Monday due to a technical fault, as Dawn reported, citing the ISPR, the official media wing of the Pakistan armed forces.The Pakistan army identified the deceased as Major Husnain Shehzad Humayun, an instructor, and Captain Abdul Samad, a trainee pilot.The aircraft crashed near Nawan Killi in Quetta.In June, a Mi-17 helicopter belonging to the Pakistan army's aviation wing crashed during take-off near Muzaffarabad in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), reportedly due to a technical fault.All personnel on board were killed. The ISPR said rescue and recovery teams were rushed to the site and an inquiry was ordered to determine the cause of the crash, Dawn reported.In September last year, five crew members died when a Pakistan army helicopter crashed in the Diamer district of Pakistan-occupied Gilgit-Baltistan (PoGB). The ISPR said the helicopter had encountered a technical fault.In August 2025, five crew members were also killed when a Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government helicopter carrying flood relief supplies crashed in a tribal district, Pakistan-based daily The Express Tribune reported.
Article Summary: Pakistan army identifies the deceased as Major Husnain Shehzad Humayun, an instructor, and Captain Abdul Samad, a trainee pilot. The aircraft crashed near Nawan Killi in Quetta. In June, a Mi-17 helicopter belonging to the Pakistan army's aviation wing crashed during take-off in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

Article Title: Graft charges at home, arrest in Qatar: Former Bangladesh Air Force chief held
Article Text:
Who is ACM (retd) Sheikh Abdul Hannan

(With PTI inputs)

Air chief marshal (retd) Sheikh Abdul Hannan of the Bangladesh Air Force was arrested in Qatar in connection with corruption charges against him in Bangladesh, an official in Dhaka said on Sunday.Akhtarul Islam, deputy director of Bangladesh’s Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), said Interpol had informed the anti-graft agency that Hannan was arrested by Qatari authorities on Thursday.“We have been informed by Interpol that Qatar’s law enforcement agency detained him there on October 15,” Islam told reporters in Dhaka.According to Islam, Hannan is accused of accumulating assets worth more than Tk 3.28 crore beyond his known sources of income and conducting suspicious transactions totalling Tk 27.63 crore through six personal bank accounts.Based on its findings, the ACC in July last year approved the filing of charges under the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, Money Laundering Prevention Act and Prevention of Corruption Act.The former air chief's wife is also an accused in the case. She allegedly accumulated assets worth more than Tk 1.91 crore beyond her known sources of income, with her husband’s assistance.The ACC identified suspicious transactions totalling Tk 1.18 crore across 32 bank accounts held in her name.Investigators have traced Hannan’s alleged offshore wealth to Canada and Dubai and uncovered assets registered in the names of his children in three countries.In March, a Dhaka court ordered the seizure of income tax records belonging to Hannan and his wife following two separate applications by the ACC.According to the agency, Hannan managed to leave Bangladesh despite an active travel ban and several corruption cases against him.A court had also ordered the attachment of two apartments owned by the former air chief and the freezing of his bank accounts after the ACC accused him of accumulating wealth beyond his known sources of income.Hannan was commissioned into the Bangladesh Air Force in 1984 as a general duty (GD) pilot. He assumed office as the force’s 16th Chief of Air Staff on June 12, 2021, and retired on June 11, 2024.As per media reports, former Bangladesh Navy chief Admiral Mohammad Nazmul Hassan also faces corruption cases and is currently abroad, although no court has imposed a travel ban on him.Both Hannan and Hassan were appointed as service chiefs during the tenure of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League government. Sheikh Hasina resigned as PM and left Bangladesh in August 2024 amid student-led public protests against her government.Hannan completed his tenure under the Awami League government, while Hassan retired during the subsequent interim administration led by Muhammad Yunus.
Article Summary: Air chief marshal (retd) Sheikh Abdul Hannan of the Bangladesh Air Force was arrested in Qatar in connection with corruption charges against him in Bangladesh. Hannan is accused of accumulating assets worth more than Tk 3.28 crore beyond his known sources of income.

Article Title: 'You are ruining entire town': With pistol in hand, Bangladesh minister raids drug den; watch
Article Text:
Bangladesh minister Ishraque Hossain raids a suspected drug den in Dhaka with a pistol in hand, sparking debate on social media

A Bangladeshi minister triggered a debate on social media after carrying out a raid on a suspected drug den in a Dhaka slum on Saturday, armed with a pistol and accompanied by associates, at least one of whom was also seen carrying a handgun.State minister for liberation war affairs Ishraque Hossain shared a video of the raid, showing him stepping out of a vehicle with a megaphone in one hand and a pistol in the other before chasing a group of people near Gandaria Railway Station.“You are ruining the entire town, destroying the entire area,” Hossain, 39, was heard telling the group in the footage, news agency PTI reported.Some of the men detained by his associates claimed they were innocent. “Let police come, then there will be talks,” Hossain was heard responding.Police said the minister had not informed them about the raid beforehand. He and his associates detained six people and handed them over to the local police station, according to officials."The minister did not inform us about the raid in advance; we learned about it afterwards,” Dhaka metropolitan police’s additional deputy commissioner Masud Rana told reporters.Hossain, a member of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), was elected to Parliament from the area in the February 12 elections.He posted the video on social media with the caption, “Ishraque's Action: Drug dens smashed and dealers handed over to the police.” The post also said he had previously conducted anti-drug raids in parts of his downtown Dhaka constituency and vowed to continue the campaign to make the area drug-free.Gendaria police station officer-in-charge Moniruzzaman Monir said officers went to the location after being informed that the men had been detained.“They detained six people and claimed they were drug abusers, so we went and brought them in,” he said.“Some powder was found in their possession, which will be tested to find out if the substance is a drug,” he added.
Article Summary: Ishraque Hossain shares video of raid on suspected drug den in Dhaka slum. Video shows him with megaphone in one hand, pistol in the other. He and associates detain six people and hand them over to local police station.

Article Title: Nepal PM, president stress unity and social harmony in Dashain messages
Article Text:
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah and President Ramchandra Paudel share heartfelt festive wishes for Bada Dashain, underlining family cohesion and social harmony. (Pic Credit: IANS)

PM remembers victims of devastating floods

President Paudel stresses harmony and cultural identity

Nepal Prime minister Balendra Shah and president Ramchandra Paudel on Saturday conveyed their greetings to the people on Bada Dashain, also known as Vijaya Dashami , the country's biggest festival, highlighting its importance in fostering family ties, social harmony and national unity.Their messages were issued on Phulpati, the seventh day of the 15-day Dashain festival. The occasion signals the start of the main festive period, when government offices close and celebrations gather momentum across Nepal.In his message, Prime Minister Shah said his government was committed to generating employment opportunities and promoting prosperity within the country so that Nepalis would not be compelled to travel abroad in search of work, according to the news agency PTI.Describing Bada Dashain as a festival that brings families together, Shah said it strengthens relationships, encourages unity and fosters closer bonds among people. He noted that the festival's religious, cultural and social significance had also helped connect Nepalis living across different parts of the world.“The sky itself feels different, the earth carries a unique fragrance, and the surroundings become naturally filled with joy and exuberance,” he said, describing the festive atmosphere.Shah observed that Nepalis had continued to celebrate Dashain and preserve their religious, cultural and social traditions despite numerous challenges over the years.Referring to the recent devastating flash floods in Bhotekoshi, Shah said this year's festivities had arrived while the country was still mourning the loss of lives and damage caused by the disaster. The floods left 1,455 people dead, 5,285 missing and more than 13,000 rescued, according to the figures cited in his message.The prime minister offered prayers for those who lost their lives, wished the injured a speedy recovery and expressed condolences to the affected families. He added that the government was working urgently to rehabilitate people displaced by the disaster.Shah also highlighted the traditional exchange of tika and jamara during Dashain. Tika, a mixture of vermilion powder, curd and rice, and jamara, consisting of barley shoots, are received from elders as symbols of respect for senior family members and affection for younger relatives.Nepalis traditionally receive tika and jamara from elders on Dashami, the festival's tenth day, which falls on October 21 this year.In a separate message, president Ramchandra Paudel extended his wishes for happiness, peace, prosperity, good health and continued progress to Nepalis living both within the country and abroad.Paudel said that while Nepal's diverse ethnic and religious communities follow their own customs and traditions, Bada Dashain plays a significant role in bringing families together and promoting social harmony, forgiveness, goodwill and fraternity.He added that the festival helps strengthen unity across Nepal's geographical, cultural and linguistic diversity while safeguarding the country's cultural identity.
Article Summary: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah and President Ramchandra Paudel send their greetings to the people on Bada Dashain. The messages were issued on Phulpati, the seventh day of the 15-day Dashain festival. The occasion signals the start of the main festive period.

Article Title: Afghanistan's lost five years under Taliban: Girls out of school, women out of work, millions hungry
Article Text:
Five years of Taliban rule in Afghanistan

Deepening crisis for Afghan women

Living with over 100 decrees: How Afghan women are walking on eggshells

Five years, countless restrictions: Afghanistan’s shrinking world
